Lose
LOOZ
v.
Webster 1828 prints LOSE as verb transitive (to mislay; to forfeit; not to gain; to be deprived of; to waste; to ruin) and as verb intransitive (not to win; to decline). Preterit and participle lost. This page keeps two longer senses in one spelling: to be deprived or to waste, and to lose life for Christ's sake. Companion pages already treat life, soul, and world.

Biblical Definition

Lose is one spelling with two honest senses. Do not mash them.

1. To be deprived; to forfeit; to waste; not to keep. To lose is to part with a thing so as not to know where it is, to forfeit in contest, to suffer waste, to throw away. Salt that has lost its savor is Webster's own biblical example. Loss is real. It is not automatically martyrdom.

2. To lose life and find it. Jesus says, whoever desires to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake will find it. What profit is it to gain the world and lose the soul. The dictionary therefore keeps lose from becoming a pep-talk. Some losses are judgment. Some are discipleship. The cross decides which.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828: LOSE, verb transitive — to mislay; to forfeit; not to gain; to be deprived of; to suffer waste; to ruin; to wander from; to waste; to throw away. LOSE, verb intransitive — not to win; to decline. Preterit and participle lost.

expand to see more

LOSE, verb transitive looz. preterit tense and participle passive lost.

1. To mislay; to part or be separated from a thing, so as to have no knowledge of the place where it is.

2. To forfeit by unsuccessful contest; as, to lose money in gaming.

3. Not to gain or win; as, to lose a battle, that is, to be defeated.

4. To be deprived of.

5. To forfeit, as a penalty. Our first parents lost the favor of God by their apostasy.

6. To suffer diminution or waste of. If the salt hath lost its savor, wherewith shall it be salted?

10. To possess no longer; to be deprived of; contrary to keep.

12. To waste; to squander; to throw away.

18. to fail to obtain. He shall in no wise lose his reward.

LOSE, verb intransitive looz.

1. To forfeit any thing in contest; not to win.

2. To decline; to fail.

Key Scripture

Matthew 16:25 — "For whoever desires to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake will find it."

Matthew 16:26 — "For what profit is it to a man if he gains the whole world, and loses his own soul? Or what will a man give in exchange for his soul?"

Modern Corruption

Lose is corrupted when self-preservation is baptized as wisdom, when losing the soul is treated as a branding risk, and when 'you can't lose' is sold as faith.

expand to see more

The first corruption is the saved self. Matthew 16:25 is whoever desires to save his life will lose it. The age catechizes men to protect the brand, the brand of me. Jesus calls that the losing.

The second corruption is world-gain as scoreboard. Matthew 16:26 still asks what profit it is to gain the whole world and lose the soul. Career religion treats the soul as a rounding error.

The third corruption is prosperity's 'you can't lose.' Webster knew losing as forfeiture and waste. Faith is not a hedge fund. Some men lose because they gambled. Some lose because they followed Christ. Do not mash those.

Usage

"Do not trade the soul for the world and call it winning (Matthew 16:26)."

"Do not mash waste with discipleship, and do not call self-preservation faith."
